title: Window width is bounded by space used
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be an alphabet, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine, and let $x$ be an input word. Suppose that at time $t$, for some integer start coordinate $a$ and natural width $n$, the window is positive in width, contains every work-head position at time $t$ and throughout the history up to $t$, has blank tape cells outside it at time $t$, and every coordinate in it has been visited by a work-tape head by time $t$. If $n\le 2t+1$, then $n$ is at most the total space used by $M$ on input $x$ through time $t$.
hypotheses_covered: $\Gamma$ is an alphabet; $M$ is a finite Turing machine; $x$ is an input word.
$t,n$ are natural numbers and $a$ is an integer.
There is a positive-width window of width $n$.
At time $t$, every work-head position lies in $[a,a+n)$.
At time $t$, every work-tape cell outside $[a,a+n)$ is blank.
Every coordinate in $[a,a+n)$ has been visited by some work-tape head by time $t$.
At every time through $t$, every work-head position lies in $[a,a+n)$.
